column2: Such and many other immeasurable deeds were done by the wise Baladeva, Shesha, supporter of the earth.
Krishna too, angry, took a handful of eraka reeds; for killing them it became an iron club at that moment.
With it that aggressor killed all the Yadavas, and others too, suddenly coming, killed one another.
Then through the middle of the ocean the victorious chariot of the discus-bearer was carried off by horses, as Daruka looked on, best of Brahmins.
The discus, mace, Sharnga bow, quivers, conch and sword circumambulated him and went by the sun's path.
In a moment there the destruction of the Yadavas occurred, except for the mighty-armed Krishna and Daruka, best of Brahmins.
Wandering, the two saw Rama seated at the foot of a tree and a great serpent coming out of his mouth.
Coming out of his mouth, that great-bodied serpent went to the ocean, worshipped by Siddhas and serpents.
The ocean, taking arghya, then went to meet him and he entered its water, worshipped by the best of serpents. Seeing Bala's departure, Keshava said to Daruka:

Tell all this to Vasudeva and Ugrasena: Baladeva's departure and the destruction of the Yadavas.
brahmapuran:210:54	I too, abiding in yoga, will give up this body. And let the people of Dvaraka and Ahuka be told:
brahmapuran:210:55	'The sea will flood this entire city; therefore, with chariots well prepared, await Arjuna's coming.
brahmapuran:210:56	Do not stay in the middle of Dvaraka when the Pandava has come out; go with him wherever that Kaurava goes.'
brahmapuran:210:57	Go and tell the son of Kunti, Arjuna, my words: 'This people who are in my charge are to be protected by you with your power.
brahmapuran:210:58	Thus with Arjuna you should take the people out of Dvaravati; and Vajra will be king of the Yadavas.'
Honouring the Brahmin's word, what Durvasas had said, he became joined in yoga, placing his foot on his knee, sages.
Then there came a hunter named Jara, holding an excellent arrow of the remaining iron of the pestle.
Seeing that foot standing like a deer, he pierced it with that very arrow, best of Brahmins.
Going up, he saw a four-armed man there, bowed to him and said again and again, "Be gracious.
This was done by me unknowingly, thinking it a deer; forgive it. Burnt by my own sin, you ought not to burn me."
Then the revered one said to him: "You have no fear at all. Go, hunter, by my grace to the abode of the lord of heaven."
At once, immediately after his words, a vehicle arrived; mounting it, the hunter went to heaven by his grace.
When he had gone, the revered one, joining himself in the self which is Brahman, imperishable, inconceivable, pure, consisting of Vasudeva,
in the unborn, ageless, indestructible, immeasurable Self of all, abandoned his human body and attained the threefold course.
While Partha looked on, the Mlecchas took the excellent women of the Vrishnis and Andhakas and went in all directions, sages.
Then the distressed Jishnu said, "Pain, pain!" and wept: "Ah, I have been abandoned by that Lord."
That bow, those weapons, that chariot, those horses — all was lost in one step like a gift to a non-Vedic Brahmin.

Ah, Fate is exceedingly strong, that without that great-souled one I, with my strength gone, have been led by low men to defeat.
brahmapuran:212:32	Those arms, that fist, that place, and I am that Arjuna; without that one, as if without merit, all has gone to worthlessness.
brahmapuran:212:33	My being Arjuna, and Bhima's being Bhima, was surely made by him; otherwise how was I defeated by cowherds without him?
Speaking thus Jishnu went to the excellent city Indraprastha and there made Vajra, the Yadava's son, king.
Then Phalguna saw Vyasa dwelling in the forest; approaching the fortunate one, he greeted him with humility.
Seeing him bowing at his feet, Vyasa said to the determined Partha, "How is it that you are so exceedingly devoid of lustre?
Have you followed a woman who is not a mother (?), or committed Brahmin-slaughter, or are you pained by the failure of hope of victory? You are now devoid of splendour.
Or were suppliants such as childless people turned away by you, or do you love a woman not to be approached, by which you have lost your lustre?
Or have you eaten a sweet dish alone without giving to Brahmins? Or have the possessions of the poor been taken by you, Arjuna?
Have you been exposed to the sun and wind, Arjuna? Or been struck by an evil eye? How else would you be without lustre?
Or have you been touched by water from a nail, or sprinkled with water from a pot, or defeated in battle by inferior persons, that you are so exceedingly without lustre?"
Then Partha, sighing, said "Hear, revered one," and being asked, Brahmins, told truly of his own defeat:

The strength, brilliance, vigour and valour that we had, the fortune and lustre — Hari has abandoned us and gone.
brahmapuran:212:44	Deprived of him, sage, who was great and spoke with a smile first, we have become like straw.
brahmapuran:212:45	The essence of weapons, arrows, the Gandiva and me, which was embodied, has gone, the Purushottama.
brahmapuran:212:46	By whose glance we had fortune, victory, wealth and elevation; that Govinda has not abandoned us, the revered one has gone abandoning us.
brahmapuran:212:47	Krishna, by whose power Bhishma, Drona, Anga's king and Duryodhana and others were burnt, has abandoned the earth.
brahmapuran:212:48	The earth seems to me, father, deprived of youth, of fortune, of lustre, and I am not alone in the absence of that discus-bearer.
brahmapuran:212:49	By whose power Bhishma and others were like moths to me, fire — without that Krishna today I have been defeated by cowherds.
brahmapuran:212:50	The Gandiva, famed in the three worlds by whose power, without him was scorned by cowherds with clubs.
brahmapuran:212:51	Many thousands of women without protectors, great sage, while I strove, were taken away by robbers with clubs as weapons.
brahmapuran:212:52	All Krishna's harem was being brought away by cowherds, taken with staff-blows, my strength overcome.
brahmapuran:212:53	It is no wonder that I am without fortune; it is a wonder that I live; I am smeared with the mire of insults from the low, shameless, grandfather.
Hearing his words, I said to the distressed and wretched great-souled Pandava, Brahmins:

Enough of your shame, Partha; you ought not to grieve. Know that such is the course of Time among all beings.
brahmapuran:212:56	Time is for the existence of beings and for their non-existence, Pandava; knowing this has Time as its root, therefore, Arjuna, be steady.
brahmapuran:212:57	Rivers, oceans, mountains, the whole earth, gods, men, animals, trees and reptiles
brahmapuran:212:58	are created by Time and again go to destruction. Knowing all this is of the nature of Time, attain peace.
brahmapuran:212:59	As you have spoken of Krishna's greatness, Dhananjaya, so it is; he descended on earth for the work of removing the burden.
brahmapuran:212:60	The earth, oppressed by burden, went in the presence of the gods formerly; for this the taker of forms at will, Janardana, has descended.
brahmapuran:212:61	That work has been accomplished; all the earth-kings were slain; and the whole Vrishni-Andhaka family has been withdrawn by Partha (Krishna).
brahmapuran:212:62	Nothing else remains to be done by him on the surface of the earth, Arjuna; so the revered one has gone, his work done, as he wished.
brahmapuran:212:63	This god of gods in creation makes creation, in preservation preservation, and at the end he is capable of burning, as he has just done.
brahmapuran:212:64	Therefore, Partha, you need not grieve at defeat; men's prowess comes at the times of becoming.
brahmapuran:212:65	By you alone were Bhishma, Drona and other kings slain; was that not an overcoming of them arisen from Time?
brahmapuran:212:66	As their defeat was by the power of Vishnu, so your arising at the end from robbers is also by the same.
brahmapuran:212:67	That god, entering other bodies, brings about the world's maintenance, and at the end the destruction of all beings, as lord of the world.
brahmapuran:212:68	At the origin of existence, son of Kunti, Janardana was your helper; at the end of existence, your opponents were looked on by Keshava.
brahmapuran:212:69	Who would believe that you killed all the Kauravas with Bhishma, or that you were defeated by cowherds?
brahmapuran:212:70	Partha, this is Hari's playful activity in all beings: that the Kauravas were destroyed by you and that you were conquered by cowherds,
brahmapuran:212:71	and that the women were taken by robbers though protected by you; that too I tell you as it was, Arjuna.
brahmapuran:212:72	Formerly there was a Brahmin named Ashtavakra, devoted to standing in water, chanting the eternal Brahman for many years, Partha.
brahmapuran:212:73	When the Asura hosts were conquered, there was a great festival on the back of Meru; the goddess-women going there saw him.
brahmapuran:212:74	Rambha, Tilottama and others, by hundreds and thousands, praised that great-souled one, Pandava, and extolled him.
brahmapuran:212:75	The sage, immersed in water up to his neck, bearing a load of matted hair — they bowed with humility, intent on praise.
brahmapuran:212:76	As he became pleased, so they praised him more, all of them, best of Kauravas, that best of the twice-born.
brahmapuran:212:77	'I am pleased, fortunate ones; ask of me whatever you desire; I shall give it, even if hard to get.'
brahmapuran:212:78	Rambha, Tilottama and the other divine apsarases said:
brahmapuran:212:79	'When you are pleased, Brahmins, what is not obtained by us?'
brahmapuran:212:80	The others said, 'Brahmin, if you, revered one, are pleased, we wish to obtain the Purushottama as husband, best of Brahmins.'
brahmapuran:212:81	Saying 'So it will be,' the sage came up out of the water. They saw him come out, ugly, eightfold crooked.
brahmapuran:212:82	Seeing him, those who were hiding laughed openly; the sage, falling into anger, cursed them, son of the Kurus:
brahmapuran:212:83	'Since you have mocked me with laughter, thinking me ugly in form, therefore I give you a curse:
brahmapuran:212:84	having obtained the Purushottama as husband by my grace, you will, struck by my curse, all go into the hands of robbers.'
brahmapuran:212:85	Hearing this, the sage was pacified by them again and said, 'You will go again to the world of the lord of gods.'
brahmapuran:212:86	Thus by the curse of the sage Ashtavakra, having obtained Keshava as husband, those excellent women fell into the hands of robbers.
brahmapuran:212:87	Therefore, Pandava, you should have not even a little grief here; by the very Lord of all that was all withdrawn.
brahmapuran:212:88	And making your withdrawal near, he has withdrawn your strength, brilliance, valour and greatness.
brahmapuran:212:89	For the born death is fixed, and for the exalted a fall; separation ends in union, and accumulation in decay.
brahmapuran:212:90	Those who, knowing this, do not feel grief or joy — others learn conduct from them; there are such people.
brahmapuran:212:91	Therefore, best of men, knowing this, with your brothers, abandoning the entire kingdom, you should go to the forest for austerity.
brahmapuran:212:92	So go, tell this my word to Dharmaraja; the day after tomorrow with your brothers do as you see fit, hero.
Thus told, he went to Dharmaraja and said all that he had seen and experienced, fully.
And all, hearing Vyasa's word reported by Arjuna, established Parikshit in the kingdom and the sons of Pandu went to the forest.
Thus, best of sages, this has been told by me in detail: the birth in the Yadu line and the deeds of Vasudeva.
by divine sages rich in austerity, Siddhas, the learned, and the holiest royal sages, Gandharvas and hosts of Apsarases,
the teacher of the moving and unmoving, the glorious one, surrounded by all the gods, Brahma, best of Brahman-knowers, said to the Daitya:
I am pleased with you, devotee, by this austerity, good vow-holder; choose a boon, may you be well; obtain the desire as you wish.

Neither gods, Asuras, Gandharvas, Yakshas, serpents nor Rakshasas, nor sages, angry, joined with austerity, would curse me with curses, grandfather of the world; this boon is chosen by me:
brahmapuran:213:54	not by weapon, nor missile, nor mountain, nor tree, not dry, not wet, not above, not below,
brahmapuran:213:55	only by one blow of a hand together with servants, army and vehicle,
brahmapuran:213:56	he who is able to destroy me shall be my death. May I myself be the sun, moon, wind and fire,
brahmapuran:213:57	water, atmosphere and space in all ways, I myself anger and desire, Varuna, Vasava and Yama, the giver of wealth and lord of wealth, Yaksha and lord of Kimpurushas.
These wondrous divine boons, dear, have been given to you by me; all these desires you will obtain, no doubt.
Having said so, the revered Grandfather quickly went to the Vairaja abode of Brahma, served by hosts of Brahmin sages.
Then the gods, Nagas, Gandharvas and sages, hearing of the granting of the boon, approached the Grandfather:
By this boon, revered one, that Asura will harass us; therefore be gracious quickly, lord, and think of his killing.
Revered one, of all beings the self-born, primal maker, lord, creator of oblations and funeral offerings, the unmanifest, Prakriti, the firm —
Then, hearing the word for the benefit of the world, the god Prajapati, the revered one, spoke to all the hosts of gods:
Surely, gods, he must obtain the fruit of his austerity; and at the end of the austerity the revered Vishnu will kill him.
Hearing this word of the lotus-born, all the gods went joyfully to their divine abodes.
As soon as he got the boon, he afflicted all creatures: the Daitya Hiranyakashipu, proud with the boon.
He then harassed the fortunate sages in hermitages, of firm vows, devoted to truth and dharma, self-controlled.
Having conquered the gods dwelling in heaven, the very mighty Asura, bringing the three worlds under control, lived in heaven.
When the Danava, intoxicated by the boon, wandering on earth, made Daityas worthy of sacrifice and the gods unworthy of sacrifice,
the Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas and Maruts approached Vishnu, the refuge, the mighty refuge.
The sacrifice consisting of Brahma and gods, the eternal god of Brahma, the past, future and present, the lord bowed to by the world, Narayana, the pervading god, they went to for refuge.

Save us today, lord of gods, from fear of Hiranyakashipu; you are our supreme god, you our supreme teacher.
brahmapuran:213:73	You are our supreme creator, of Brahma and the rest, best of gods; lotus-petal-eyed, pure, destroyer of the enemy side, for the destruction of the Diti's line be our refuge.

Give up fear, immortals; I give you fearlessness. You will regain heaven, gods, soon.
brahmapuran:213:75	Here I am; I shall kill that Daitya with his host, proud with his boon, unslayable by lords of immortals, the lord of Danavas.
Having said so, the revered one, dismissing the lords of the thirty, the very mighty one came to Hiranyakashipu's place.
Making half his body a man's and half a lion's, the lord, in the Narasimha form, touching his hand with hand,
dark as dense cloud, with a voice like dense cloud, with radiance like dense cloud, swift like a cloud,
seeing the extremely strong Daitya, with the valour of a proud tiger, he killed him, guarded by proud hosts of Daityas, with one hand.
This Narasimha has been told; hear again another, Vamana, in which, taking Vamana's form, the destroyer of Daityas
at the sacrifice of the mighty Bali formerly, the great Asuras who were unshakable by Vishnu with his three strides were shaken:
Vipracitti, Shiva, Shanku, Ayahshanku, Ayahshira, Ashvashira, and the mighty Hayagriva,
Vegavan, Ketuman, Ugra, Sogravyagra the great Asura, Pushkara and Pushkala, Shashva, and Ashvapati,
Prahlada, Ashvapati, Kumbha, Samhrada, Gamanapriya, Anuhrada, Harihaya, Varaha, Samhara, Anuja,
Sharabha, Shalabha, Kupatha, Krodhana, Kratha, Brihatkirti, Mahajihva, Shankukarna, Mahasvana,
Diptajihva, Arkanayana, Mrigapada, Mrigapriya, Vayu, Garishtha, Namuchi, Sambara, Viskara the great,
Chandrahanta, Krodhahanta, Krodhavardhana, Kalaka, Kalakopa, Vritra, Krodha, Virochana,
Garishtha, Varishtha, Pralamba and Naraka, Indratapana, Vatapi, Ketuman, proud of strength,
Asiloma, Puloma, Bashkala, Pramada, Mada, Svamishra, Kalavadana, Karala, Keshi,
Ekaksha, Chandrama, Rahu, Samhrada, Sambara, Svana, holders of shataghnis and discuses in hand, and pestle-handed,
armed with horse-machines and weapons, with bhindipalas, with spears and mortars in hand, with axes,
with nooses and hammers in hand, with clubs in hand, with great rocks as weapons, the Danavas with spears in hand,
terrible, with many weapons, in many guises, very mighty, with faces of tortoises and cocks, hares and owls,
with faces of asses and camels, boars, cats, peacocks and great faces, others,
heroes with faces of crocodiles and rams, cows, goats, buffaloes, with faces of iguanas and porcupines and jackals, the Danavas,
with faces of rats and frogs, terrible, with wolf faces, fearsome, with makara faces and heron faces, the Danavas,
with horse faces, ass faces, peacock faces, wearing the hides of king-elephants and black antelope skins,
with bodies covered by bark, and wearing blue garments, turbaned, crowned, with earrings, the Asuras,
wearing diadems, long-crested, conch-necked, of fine lustre, Daityas in many dresses, with many garlands and unguents,
taking their own weapons blazing with brilliance, surrounded Hrishikesha on all sides as he strode.
Having crushed all the Daityas with the soles of his feet and hands, the Lord took a very terrible form and quickly seized the earth.
As he strode over the earth, the moon and sun stood between his breasts; as he strode across the sky, they stood at his navel;
as he strode beyond, they stood at his knee region; so the twice-born say of Vishnu of immeasurable valour.
Having seized the entire earth and killed the foremost Asuras, Vishnu, best of the mighty, gave the earth to Shakra.
This is your Vamana, the manifestation of the great-souled one; this is told by Veda-knowing Brahmins as the Vaishnava glory.
Again there is the manifestation of the great-souled Vishnu, the Self of beings, famed as Dattatreya, endowed with supreme forbearance;
by him, when the Vedas were lost and the procedures and sacrifices, and the four varnas mixed, and dharma had grown lax —
